papers.abstract_en: Background: Dirozalkib is a highly selective anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) inhibitor with intracranial antitumor activity against crizotinib-resistant mutations. This phase III trial evaluated dirozalkib versus crizotinib in patients with ALK inhibitor-naïve, ALK-positive, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Methods: In this multicenter, randomized, open-label DIAMOND-2 trial, adult patients with ALK inhibitor-naïve, ALK-positive, advanced NSCLC who either had received no prior systemic therapy or had experienced disease progression or intolerance after one prior chemotherapy regimen were randomly assigned 1:1 to dirozalkib (500 mg once daily) or crizotinib (250 mg twice daily). The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival (PFS). Results: Between 2022 January 24 and 2023 April 30, 275 patients were randomly assigned to receive dirozalkib (n = 137) or crizotinib (n = 138). As of 2025 May 31, the median follow-up durations were 32.8 and 31.6 months, respectively. Median investigator-assessed PFS was 29.5 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 20.3 to not reached) months with dirozalkib versus 12.9 (95% CI = 11.1 to 17.6) months with crizotinib (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.47, 95% CI = 0.34 to 0.66; P < 0.001). Blinded-independent-central-review-assessed PFS was also significantly prolonged with dirozalkib (median PFS, 27.5 versus 12.9 months; HR = 0.54, 95% CI = 0.39 to 0.74; P < 0.001). Grade ≥3 treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were less frequent with dirozalkib than with crizotinib (60.6% versus 72.5%), and TEAEs led to treatment discontinuation in 2.2% and 7.2% of patients, respectively. Conclusions: Dirozalkib significantly improved PFS versus crizotinib, with a manageable safety profile, supporting its use as a first-line therapy for ALK-positive advanced NSCLC. Trial registration: This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov on 2022 January 24 (NCT05204628).

papers.abstract_en: Although EGFR inhibitors are highly effective for treating EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinomas (EGFR+ LUADs), resistance inevitably emerges, with histologic transformation to small cell lung cancer (SCLC) representing a particularly aggressive mechanism. Our prospective trial enrolled patients with EGFR+ LUAD at high risk of transformation (TP53/RB1-deficient) and treated them with first-line osimertinib combined with platinum and etoposide. Despite the addition of SCLC-directed chemotherapy, nearly half of patients (5 of 11) underwent SCLC transformation, with median progression-free survival of 11 months and overall survival of 33 months. Genomic and single-cell transcriptomic profiling of patient samples revealed clinical and subclinical plasticity associated with TP53/RB1 comutations, including histological transformation to SCLC, as well as mesenchymal and squamous histologies. These changes in plasticity were linked to progressive disruption of the RB pathway, leading to altered chromatin accessibility and induction of neuronal differentiation and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition transcriptional programs, further intensified by osimertinib treatment. These findings provide insights into the role of plasticity in mediating drug tolerance.

papers.abstract_en: Background: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based chemoimmunotherapy has become a standard first-line treatment for patients with driver-negative metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but the clinical benefit is limited. Radiotherapy has potential antitumor immunomodulatory effects, but the optimal dose and fractionation remain unclear. Methods: This single-arm, multicenter, prospective, phase II trial enrolled patients with stage IV driver-negative NSCLC who received first-line chemoimmunotherapy. During the ICI maintenance phase, patients received hybrid dose-fraction radiotherapy (Hybrid-RT): stereotactic ablative body radiotherapy (SABR) to targetable lesions and low-dose radiotherapy (LDRT) to other sites. Patients restaged to stage III disease after chemoimmunotherapy received short-course hypofractionated radiotherapy to all residual lesions. The primary endpoint was 1-year progression-free survival (PFS) rate. The secondary endpoints included 1-year overall survival (OS) rate, objective response rate, and safety. Parallel preclinical mechanistic studies were performed in a murine model. Results: A total of 83 patients were enrolled from 2022 May 9 to 2023 December 31. The 1-year PFS rate was 54.2% (median PFS 16.1 months; 95% confidence interval [CI] 11.4 to 19.2 months), meeting the primary endpoint. The 1-year OS rate was 83.1% (median OS 29.3 months; 95% CI 21.9 months to not reached), and treatment was well tolerated. Peripheral immune profiling showed posttreatment expansion of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and natural killer (NK) cells associated with promising clinical efficacy. In the murine model, ICI plus Hybrid-RT (IHBRT) induced a division of labor between CD8+ T and NK cells. At LDRT lesions, it facilitated both C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (Cxcr3)-mediated recruitment of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and natural killer group 2 member D-mediated NK cell cytotoxicity. At SABR lesions, Cxcr3-mediated CD8+ T cells played a predominant role, whereas NK cells contributed minimally. Moreover, IHBRT suppressed secreted phosphoprotein 1 positive (Spp1+) macrophages and relieved immunosuppression. Conclusions: Clinically, IHBRT demonstrates promising efficacy and a manageable safety profile in driver-negative metastatic NSCLC. Preclinically, it induces a functional division of labor between CD8+ T and NK cells to activate antitumor immune cytotoxicity, and suppresses Spp1+ macrophages, thereby relieving immunosuppression. Trial registration: This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT05348668). Date of registration: 2022 April 26.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Variable clinical remission rates on biologics may reflect heterogeneity within type 2 (T2) asthma, but such heterogeneity remains largely unexplored. OBJECTIVES: To identify clinically distinct T2 asthma subtypes using multidimensional profiling and hierarchical clustering. METHODS: All T2 participants (n=764) were from the Australasian Severe Asthma Network, identified by elevated eosinophil levels, elevated FeNO, or allergic sensitization. Baseline clinical and inflammatory data were integrated to identify potential clusters in the training set using hierarchical clustering, followed by prospective assessment of exacerbation over 12 months. A random forest classifier was internally cross-validated and applied to a held-out validation set to assess profile consistency. RESULTS: Three subtypes emerged as: Cluster 1 (n=241, 45.0%) represented a female-predominant, well-controlled allergic subtype; Cluster 2 (n=110, 20.6%) constituted older T2 asthma patients with overlapping non-T2 features, including increased sputum neutrophil counts, fixed airflow limitation, and multiple comorbidities, with higher severe exacerbation rates (incidence rate ratios [IRR]=2.54, P=0.025) and emergency visit rates (IRR=5.06, P=0.040); and Cluster 3 (n=184, 34.4%) showed multiple elevated T2 biomarkers, poor symptom control and increased severe exacerbation (IRR=2.49, P=0.007) and hospitalization risk (IRR=3.28, P=0.009). The classifier showed 83.6% agreement with the original cluster assignments (κ=0.738), with post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC, age, and BMI as leading discriminators. CONCLUSIONS: T2 asthma encompasses distinct subtypes with prognostic and therapeutic implications. Our findings support a precision medicine approach for these subtypes: Cluster 3 patients may warrant early assessment for biologic therapy when eligible, while Cluster 2 may benefit from integrated strategies addressing non-T2 traits.

papers.abstract_en: Primary pulmonary NUT carcinoma (PPNC) is an ultra-rare, highly aggressive thoracic malignancy driven by NUTM1 rearrangements, most commonly BRD4:NUTM1. Morphologic overlap with poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma, neuroendocrine carcinoma, and carcinoma not otherwise specified frequently delays diagnosis, while rapid progression and limited evidence hinder treatment standardization. This narrative review synthesizes literature identified through PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science, together with registered trials from ClinicalTrials.gov, through May 2026, covering epidemiology, molecular pathogenesis, diagnosis, locoregional therapy, systemic treatment, and investigational strategies. An exploratory descriptive analysis of 15,938 lung tumor samples from 41 independent cBioPortal datasets identified a canonical NUTM1 structural variant in 1 of 15,938 samples (0.006%), supporting the genomic rarity of PPNC and highlighting potential limitations of DNA-only workflows for clinically relevant rearrangements. PPNC is usually reported in young to middle-aged adults, appears more frequent in men, and commonly presents with nonspecific thoracic symptoms. Molecular data suggest phenotypic and transcriptional convergence with squamous cell carcinoma through BRD-NUT-driven programs centered on MYC and TP63, with context-dependent SOX2 activation. Accurate recognition requires early NUT immunohistochemistry, followed when feasible by RNA-based fusion testing. No standard systemic regimen exists. Platinum-based regimens remain common, whereas retrospective pulmonary-specific data suggest that definitive chemoradiotherapy may be preferable to chemotherapy alone in selected patients. Bromodomain and extraterminal (BET) inhibitor monotherapy shows target engagement but limited durability, supporting rational combinations. Radiotherapy-immunotherapy combinations and PRAME-directed T-cell-engaging therapies remain investigational; the latter have only preclinical support so far. Earlier diagnosis, multimodal definitive treatment, and prioritized basket-trial enrollment are essential to improve outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ivonescimab plus chemotherapy shows outstanding efficacy for advanced squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but its pharmacoeconomic value remains to be determined. Therefore, this study seeks to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of the ivonescimab regimen for advanced squamous NSCLC from the Chinese and U.S. healthcare perspectives, and to explore the theoretical cost-effective price threshold of ivonescimab. METHODS: Survival curves from the HARMONi-6 trial were fitted and extrapolated, and direct medical costs were calculated. A partitioned survival model was developed within TreeAge Pro to project disease trajectory and resource utilization over a 10-year time horizon. The primary outcome was the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER), compared against willingness-to-pay (WTP) to assess the ivonescimab regimen's cost-effectiveness. Sensitivity, scenario, and threshold analyses were performed to assess parameter uncertainty and estimate ivonescimab's theoretical cost-effective price threshold. RESULTS: In China, the ivonescimab group cost $60,942 for 2.33 QALYs versus $30,093 for 1.57 QALYs in the tislelizumab group, yielding an ICER of $40,328/QALY. Utility during progressive disease was the most influential parameter. Ivonescimab's theoretical cost-effective price thresholds were $27.85/100mg, $67.63/100mg, and $107.4/100mg, corresponding to WTPs of single, double, and triple the per-capita GDP, respectively. In the U.S., the total costs were $572,981 and $419,922, and the health outcomes were 3.16 QALYs and 2.19 QALYs for the two arms, with an ICER of $157,444/QALY. Ivonescimab's price was the dominant driver of ICER. The theoretical cost-effective price thresholds were $609.10/100 mg and $777.31/100mg, corresponding to the $100,000/QALY and $150,000/QALY WTP, respectively. CONCLUSION: Under the unified model framework of this study, compared with the tislelizumab regimen, the ivonescimab regimen as the first-line treatment for advanced squamous NSCLC in both countries is unlikely to have a cost-effectiveness advantage.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) represents the common end-stage outcome of a broad range of interstitial lung diseases. The shared pathophysiologic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify two phenotypically distinct neutrophil subsets in PF: a pro-inflammatory subset characterized by CD54 (human) or iNOS (mouse) expression, and an alternative subset marked by Arg1 expression. Notably, CD54+ and iNOS+ neutrophils were markedly expanded in PF patients and mice with bleomycin-induced PF, respectively. Adoptive transfer of iNOS+ neutrophils exacerbated fibrosis in bleomycin-induced PF, whereas transfer of Arg1+ neutrophils had no significant effect. Further, the expression of PIEZO1, a mechanically activated ion channel, is predominantly upregulated in CD54+ neutrophils from PF patients or iNOS+ neutrophils from PF mice. Piezo1 ablation in neutrophils selectively impairs iNOS+ neutrophil differentiation, thereby attenuating fibrosis progression. Mechanistically, PIEZO1 promotes the differentiation of these pro-inflammatory subsets through the transcription factor IRF4 in a calcium-dependent manner. We further identify the JAK/STAT pathway as an upstream regulator of PIEZO1 expression in neutrophils. Consequently, PIEZO1 expression and CD54+ neutrophils are markedly decreased in patients treated with JAK inhibitor baricitinib. Importantly, combined inhibition of JAK/STAT and calcium signaling exerts synergistic suppression on the iNOS+ neutrophil expansion and PF progression. Together, our findings reveal a mechanism in which PIEZO1 promotes PF by specifically driving the expansion of CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophils.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Systemic inflammation plays a crucial role in cancer progression and may influence outcomes after surgical treatment. Blood count-derived inflammatory indices such as the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) have been proposed as prognostic biomarkers in several malignancies. However, their prognostic value in surgically treated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), particularly for recurrence-related outcomes, remains incompletely defined. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 132 patients with histologically confirmed NSCLC who underwent curative-intent anatomical lung resection between January 2022 and December 2025. Preoperative inflammatory markers (NLR, PLR, SII) were calculated from blood counts obtained within 14 days before surgery. Associations with clinicopathologic features, postoperative complications, and disease-free survival (DFS) were assessed using non-parametric tests, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox proportional hazards regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. RESULTS: The median age was 64.5 years and 64.4% of patients were male. Adenocarcinoma cases demonstrated higher lymphocyte counts and lower PLR compared with non-adenocarcinoma tumors. Inflammatory indices increased significantly with advancing tumor size-based T category. During follow-up, 20 DFS events were observed. In univariable Cox regression, higher log-transformed NLR (HR 2.34, 95% CI 1.09-5.01; p = 0.029), PLR (HR 2.56, 95% CI 1.12-5.89; p = 0.027), and SII (HR 2.06, 95% CI 1.14-3.74; p = 0.017) were associated with shorter DFS. In the primary multivariable model, logNLR remained associated with recurrence risk (adjusted HR 2.18, 95% CI 1.01-4.72; p = 0.046). In a pre-specified Firth penalized stage-adjusted sensitivity analysis, this association was attenuated and no longer statistically significant (adjusted HR 2.05, 95% CI 0.94-4.44), indicating substantial overlap between NLR and tumour stage. ROC analysis demonstrated moderate predictive performance of NLR for DFS events (AUC 0.67). An exploratory cutoff analysis suggested that NLR values above 2.0 were associated with worse DFS. CONCLUSION: Preoperative systemic inflammatory indices are associated with tumor burden and disease-free survival in surgically treated NSCLC. Among the evaluated markers, NLR demonstrated the most consistent prognostic signal. These findings support further investigation of inflammation-based biomarkers as adjunct tools for recurrence risk stratification in operable lung cancer. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: We confirm that our study is not a clinical trial. "Clinical trial number not applicable."

papers.abstract_en: Pleural fluid biomarkers are increasingly being investigated as tools for evaluating challenging pleural effusions. Nevertheless, a substantial proportion of patients remain without a definitive diagnosis despite cytology, microbiology, pleural biopsy and clinical follow-up. Most pleural diagnostic studies exclude these unresolved cases, potentially introducing spectrum, selection and verification biases, as well as overly optimistic estimates of test performance. In this perspective article, we examine the methodological implications of handling unresolved pleural effusions in pleural research. We discuss the limitations of complete-case analyses and review alternative strategies, including intention-to-diagnose frameworks, composite reference standards, longitudinal follow-up, probabilistic adjudication, multiple imputation, sensitivity analyses and latent class models. Rather than arbitrarily excluding unresolved pleural effusions, future pleural studies should explicitly acknowledge and model diagnostic uncertainty to generate more clinically relevant and generalisable estimates of test performance.

papers.abstract_en: Most genome-wide association studies (GWASs) and polygenic score (PGS) models for lung function are based on European-ancestry individuals. Here, we performed GWASs in 17,738 Chinese individuals from the Dongfeng-Tongji (DFTJ) and Wuhan-Zhuhai (WHZH) cohorts, followed by meta-analysis with lung function GWASs from the China Kadoorie Biobank (sample size, n = 100,285), the Taiwan Biobank (n = 62,901), and European-ancestry studies (n = 400,102). Multi-ancestry fine-mapping pinpoints four novel candidate causal variants: one insertion (rs56381615, LINC02270) and three SNPs (rs6941411, PTK7; rs13315867, EPHA3; and rs2713769, ABI3BP). Cross-ancestry genetic correlations are high (0.682-0.811) but significantly lower than 1 (p < 0.005). Transcriptome-wide association analysis across 16 tissues identifies 1,374 genes, including PTK7, CUL7, and EPHA3 as leading novel candidates. Finally, we develop multi-ancestry PGS models that outperform existing models. Overall, this study quantifies cross-ancestry genetic correlation, prioritizes candidate genes, and enhances PGS prediction accuracy of lung function traits in East Asian populations.

papers.abstract_en: Lung function evaluation is rapidly evolving beyond laboratory testing. While conventional tests remain the clinical reference standard, digital health technologies now enable respiratory assessment at home and in real-world settings through home-based systems, portable devices, and wearables. These tools can support repeated or continuous monitoring of traditional and digital biomarkers of respiratory health and disease. However, they differ in physiological detail, usability, degree of patient involvement and clinical maturity. In parallel, artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming an important complement to these technologies. Machine learning and deep learning can support signal processing, quality control and interpretation of pulmonary function tests, while also extracting clinically relevant information from multimodal respiratory data collected outside controlled environments. Generative AI has a more emerging role, mainly in patient communication and educational support. For pulmonary function test interpretation, current evidence supports clinician-AI collaboration as the most realistic near-term model, rather than fully autonomous decision-making. This review summarises the main technologies currently available for lung function evaluation in adults and discusses the current and future role of AI in respiratory monitoring, interpretation and personalised care.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) greatly influences clinical management and therapeutic decision-making in patients with cancer. Accurate differentiation between MPE and non-MPE is therefore essential. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of traditional ultrasonographic signs and ultrasound findings of adjacent thoracic structures in identifying MPE. METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Embase were searched until 2 May 2025 to identify studies evaluating the diagnostic accuracy of ultrasonographic signs using traditional ultrasound (TrUS) and shear wave elastography (SWE) for detecting MPE. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, diagnostic odds ratio, predictive values and likelihood ratios were estimated using a random-effects model. RESULTS: 10 studies fulfilled the eligibility criteria, including nine evaluating TrUS and three investigating SWE. Several ultrasonographic signs were highly specific for MPE, including pleural nodules (99%), diaphragmatic nodules (96%) and pleural thickening (93%). Concomitant chest wall invasion, hepatic metastasis and lung consolidation showed near-absolute specificity (99-100%). Nevertheless, the sensitivity of these signs did not exceed 60%. Meanwhile, SWE showed balanced diagnostic performance, with sensitivity ranging from 76.36% to 100% and specificity ranging from 59.09% to 94.40%, depending on the cut-off values used. CONCLUSION: TrUS can be considered in the working diagnosis of MPE, as pleural and diaphragmatic nodules, pleural thickening, chest wall invasion, lung involvement and liver metastasis show high specificity for MPE. However, further studies are needed to investigate the role of SWE in diagnosing MPE.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: The RDRio genotype of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB), a major genotype within the Latin American-Mediterranean (LAM) family, has been associated with increased transmissibility and multidrug resistance (MDR). In Ecuador, a previous baseline study reported a low prevalence of 2.09% for 2012-2016, prior to the large influx of migrants from Venezuela-where RDRio is highly endemic-that has occurred since 2015. This study aimed to update the molecular epidemiology of the RDRio genotype in Ecuador. METHODS: We screened 699 clinical MTB isolates collected in 2018 (384) and 2023 (315) for the RDRio genotype by duplex PCR and further characterized them by 24-locus MIRU-VNTR typing, spoligotyping, and whole-genome sequencing (WGS). We conducted minimum spanning tree (MST) analyses based on MIRU-VNTR profiles to assess genetic relatedness. RESULTS: We identified 40 isolates (5.72%) as RDRio, with no significant difference in prevalence between 2018 (n = 20; 5.21%) and 2023 (n = 20; 6.35%). WGS confirmed that the dominant sublineages were 4.3.4.1 and 4.3.4.2, all within Lineage 4 (Euro-American). Genotypic resistance profiling classified 32.1% (9/28) of sequenced isolates as MDR-TB and 7.1% (2/28) as pre-XDR-TB. MST analysis showed that RDRio isolates from Ecuador segregated predominantly into distinct clonal complexes and remained largely isolated from international reference strains, including Venezuelan isolates. DISCUSSION: The overall RDRio prevalence of 5.72% represents a nearly three-fold increase relative to the 2.09% reported for the 2012-2016 baseline, although it remained stable across the 2018-2023 period and low compared with high-endemicity settings such as Venezuela. Despite this relatively low prevalence, the RDRio genotype was associated with a substantial burden of drug resistance. The genetic segregation of the predominant RDRio Ecuadorian clonal complex from international reference strains-including Venezuelan isolates-did not support recent importation associated with the Venezuelan diaspora. Despite their limitations, classical genotyping methods remain a valid, cost-effective approach to monitor MTB strains of interest associated with MDR-TB, such as RDRio, in low-resource settings like Ecuador.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The treatment of NTM pulmonary disease is hindered by scarce therapeutic options. Bedaquiline is a diarylquinoline with activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis and a variety of pathogenic nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) that could help fill this unmet need, but clinical data are needed to support its use. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the use of bedaquiline in patients with NTM pulmonary disease from National Jewish Health and the University of Texas Health Science Center Tyler between the years of 2013 and 2022. RESULTS: Eighty-seven patients were included in the study. Most patients were female (66/87, 75.8%) and the mean age was 55 years. 54% had cavitary lung disease. People with cystic fibrosis made up 26.4% of the cohort. There were 46 patients with Mycobacterium avium complex, 36 patients with Mycobacterium abscessus and five patients with other mycobacterial infections. 64% of isolates had macrolide resistance, either inducible or mutational, 31% had amikacin resistance (MIC ≥ 64 𝜇g/ml) and 21.8% had both macrolide and amikacin resistance. The mean duration of antibiotic use prior to the initiation of bedaquiline was 32.8 months (0-165 months). The most common indication for bedaquiline use was treatment failure related to intolerance or resistance to antibiotics. Mean duration of bedaquiline use was 20 months (range 1-134 mos.). Bedaquiline was well tolerated: only 10% (9/87) of patients required discontinuation of treatment related to side effects of whom 4 reported adverse events related to bedaquiline, one with a rash, one with nausea and two with transaminase elevation. None of the patients discontinued therapy related to QTc prolongation. Ten patients had to discontinue bedaquiline due to lack of insurance coverage, although the mean exposure to bedaquiline in this group was 18 months (2-43 mo.) Once on bedaquiline, 46% had sputum cultures convert to negative (defined as two negative cultures over three months) and 40% were able to discontinue all therapy with 12 months of negative cultures. CONCLUSION: In this cohort of treatment experienced patients with drug resistance or intolerance, bedaquiline was well-tolerated and led to cure in 40% of patients.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Accurate prediction of long-term readmission risk is crucial for early intervention in patients experiencing severe acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (s-AECOPD). While the Chronic Respiratory Early Warning Score (CREWS) has demonstrated proficiency in predicting severe outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of CREWS in predicting readmission for s-AECOPD. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This study conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of all hospitalized s-AECOPD patients from 2018 to 2019. Follow-up occurred from 2020 to 2021. Clinical parameters were collected. Patients were classified according to hospitalization frequency during the follow-up period and clinical parameters were compared between the groups. Logistic regression, ROC analysis and survival analysis were performed. RESULTS: A total of 301 patients were included in the cohort study, of whom 56 were classified into the non-decreased hospitalization frequency group. High serum uric acid (UA) levels and low free thyroxine (FT4) levels could be independent risk factors associated with s-AECOPD long-term readmission (OR 6.125 (1.775-21.131), p = 0.004 ; OR 2.599 (1.244-5.432), p = 0.010, respectively). The modified CREWS model demonstrated moderate predictive performance for readmission (AUC = 0.716, 95%CI 0.628-0.805, H-L = 0.287, p < 0.001). Patients with a modified-CREWS score over 8 faced an elevated risk of mortality within two years (p = 0.008). CONCLUSION: Elevated serum UA levels and decreased FT4 levels are independent risk factors for s-AECOPD readmission. The modified-CREWS tool demonstrated acceptable discrimination for predicting both s-AECOPD readmission and mortality.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Orofacial myofunctional therapy (OMT) is a promising treatment for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but protocols vary and outcomes are inconsistent. The primary aim was to evaluate the effect of a standardized OMT protocol on changes in apnea-hypopnea index (AHI). Secondary aims were to analyze associations between OMT adherence and change in objective and self-reported outcomes. METHODS: Treatment-naive adults with mild-to-moderate OSA were randomized in a multicenter trial to 12 weeks of OMT or a waitlist control group. Three nights of polysomnography were completed before and after the intervention. Adherence was registered electronically. The primary outcome was change in AHI. Pre-defined secondary outcomes were changes in desaturation measures and in the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) score. Intention-to-treat analyses were performed using linear mixed-effects models, whereas per-protocol analyses were based on analysis of covariance. RESULTS: A total of 104 participants (mean age 47.1 ± 12.2 years) were included. Intention-to-treat analysis included 104 participants (52 treatment, 52 waitlist) and showed no significant effect of OMT on AHI. Difference in AHI change between groups was 0.6 (95% CI -3.3 to 4.5; P = .774). Overall mean adherence across all days and participants was 64.6% (95% CI 61.0 to 76.8). Higher adherence was not associated with significantly greater reduction in AHI (β = -0.1, 95% CI -0.2 to 0.1; P = .353). No change was detected in pre-defined secondary outcomes. CONCLUSION: Twelve weeks of standardized OMT had no significant effect on AHI, desaturation measures or ESS score in treatment-naive patients newly diagnosed with OSA. CURRENT KNOWLEDGE/STUDY RATIONALE: Orofacial myofunctional therapy (OMT) is increasingly considered a non-invasive treatment for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but existing evidence is heterogeneous and often limited by methodological shortcomings. We therefore conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effects of a standardized OMT protocol in adults newly diagnosed with mild-to-moderate OSA. STUDY IMPACT: The intervention did not improve pre-defined OSA outcomes, highlighting the importance of rigorous trials even when results are negative. These findings help refine the evidence base for OMT in adults with OSA while supporting continued investigation of alternative protocols and populations stratified by endo- or phenotyping. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The lack of perfusate metabolic homeostasis during ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP) may impair lung physiology or stability and limit the application of advanced donor lung therapies. There is evidence that additional organ support during EVLP can improve graft preservation and transplant outcomes. We hypothesized that incorporation of a kidney into an EVLP circuit would maintain perfusate homeostasis and improve lung preservation and metabolic activity. METHODS: A novel circuit was developed to allow simultaneous normothermic perfusion of lungs and kidney in parallel. Donor pig lungs underwent 12 hours of cellular EVLP (EVLP, n=5) or combined cellular ex vivo lung-kidney perfusion (EVLKP, n=5). Lung function was assessed hourly and inflammatory cytokines, edema formation, hemolysis, histologic injury, and kidney performance were evaluated. RESULTS: Simultaneous lung and kidney perfusion achieved target pulmonary and renal perfusion parameters with stable hemodynamics. EVLKP demonstrated trends of higher compliance, lower inspiratory pressure and pulmonary vascular resistance. Perfusate lactate concentration in EVLKP was markedly lower (P<0.0001), glucose concentrations were higher (P=0.0102), and pH shifted towards physiologic levels (P=0.0009) compared to EVLP. Oxygenation capacity was comparable between groups. Kidney perfusion remained stable throughout EVLKP. CONCLUSIONS: Combined ex vivo lung-kidney perfusion is safe and feasible in a large-animal model for prolonged lung perfusion. EVLKP improved perfusate homeostasis compared with EVLP alone, which is associated with trends of improvement in lung physiologic parameters. These findings suggest that kidney-derived metabolic and biological support may provide benefits beyond perfusate filtration and highlight the potential importance of organ-organ crosstalk during ex vivo perfusion.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Viral pneumonia-associated pulmonary aspergillosis (VAPA) is a lethal complication in critically ill patients. We aimed to develop a generalizable and methodologically robust prediction tool for early VAPA risk, overcoming key limitations of existing models. METHODS: In a multi-center, ambispective cohort of 4,966 patients with influenza or COVID-19 admitted to ICU (Jan 2023-Jun 2025), we developed and validated two prediction models for VAPA using LASSO-selected variables: a standard Cox proportional hazards model and a Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards model accounting for non-VAPA death as a competing risk. For both models, restricted cubic splines were used to address nonlinear associations between continuous predictors and VAPA. Performance was assessed at 7 and 14 days post-ICU admission. Subgroup analysis was employed to examine the virus-specific models' performance. RESULTS: The incidence of VAPA was 8.8%. The Fine-Gray model demonstrated excellent discrimination and calibration in both derivation and validation cohorts. In contrast, the standard Cox model substantially overestimated VAPA risk, particularly among high-risk patients (by 20-30%). Key predictors included haematological malignancy, halo sign, use of priority antibiotic combinations, SOFA score, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and pre-ICU corticosteroid dose; the latter three exhibited J-shaped associations with VAPA risk. A significant interaction was observed between viral subtype and pre-ICU corticosteroid dose (P = 0.006), with a stronger association in COVID-19 patients (sHR=1.17, 95% CI: 1.09-1.26). Overall model performance remained consistent across viral subtypes. An interactive web-based tool was then deployed, which generates both individualized VAPA risk estimates and corresponding clinical management recommendations. CONCLUSIONS: In critically ill patients with viral pneumonia, a competing-risk model accounting for non-VAPA death provides more accurate estimates of VAPA risk than traditional approaches. The model demonstrates robust generalizability across influenza and COVID-19 pneumonia and offers a practical tool for early, personalized VAPA prediction.

papers.abstract_en: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a life-threatening disorder characterized by pulmonary endothelial injury, vascular leakage, and hypoxemia, yet no targeted therapies are available to protect the lung vasculature. Dysregulated complement activation contributes to endothelial dysfunction through excessive deposition of the membrane attack complex (MAC), which disrupts endothelial barrier integrity. CD59 is a membrane-bound complement inhibitor that protects endothelial cells (ECs) from MAC-mediated injury, but its role and therapeutic potential in ALI remain unclear. In this study, we found that endothelial CD59 was significantly reduced during bacteria-induced ALI and that Cd59 deficiency exacerbated pulmonary vascular leakage in mice. To supplement endothelial CD59, we engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs) expressing lymphocyte function-associated antigen-1 (LFA-1) (EVLFA-1) to enhance delivery to activated endothelium. CD59-loaded EVs (EVLFA-1-CD59) preferentially targeted ECs, reduced endothelial MAC deposition and apoptosis, and preserved endothelial barrier integrity in experimental ALI. EVLFA-1-CD59 also improved survival following bacterial infection. Collectively, these data establish diminished endothelial CD59 levels as a critical driver of complement-driven vascular injury and highlight EVLFA-1-mediated CD59 delivery as a promising therapeutic strategy for ALI.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive, life-threatening complication of congenital heart disease (CHD). We aimed to determine the burden of clinically relevant PAH in a well-characterised adult CHD population. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 35 235 adult CHD patients from the Australian National CHD Registry, of whom 392 had clinically significant PAH (mean±sd age 43.4±13.9) (prevalence 1.11%). We prospectively defined clinically significant PAH as 1) prescription of PAH-specific therapy and/or 2) known Eisenmenger syndrome. 330 patients (84.2%) received PAH pharmacotherapy during the study period and 193 patients (49.2%) had Eisenmenger syndrome, 62 (32.1%) of whom were untreated. RESULTS: During the study period, 141 (36.0%) patients died, PAH treatment was associated with a numerically lower risk of mortality (hazard ratio (HR) 0.74, 95% CI 0.49-1.11; p=0.22). Patients with moderate complexity CHD had a significantly higher risk of death than the mild group (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.08-2.92; p=0.023), whilst severe complexity patients had >2.5 times the risk of death (p<0.001). At last follow-up, 211 (63.9%) of treated patients were prescribed monotherapy, 90 (27.3%) dual and 29 (8.8%) triple therapy. From initial treatment to last follow-up, 123 (37.3%) of the treated group had switched therapy, 100 (30.3%) died, 75 (22.7%) continued their initial pharmacotherapy, 25 (7.6%) added additional drugs and seven (2.1%) underwent transplantation. CONCLUSIONS: Approximately 1.11% of a large adult CHD population had clinically significant PAH. Mortality is high (6.9% at age 30 years, 35.7% at age 50 years) and treatment has shifted towards increased utilisation of combination therapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) comprise a diverse group of organisms that can cause pulmonary and extrapulmonary disease. Their management is challenging, because many NTM species exhibit intrinsic antimicrobial resistance; current multidrug treatment regimens have limited efficacy and tolerability; and the number of immunocompromised individuals at risk of NTM disease is increasing. Phage therapy has recently emerged as a potential therapeutic option for refractory NTM pulmonary disease (NTM-PD). This scoping review aimed to map and critically assess the existing evidence on the clinical use of phage therapy for NTM-PD and its reported outcomes. METHODS: PubMed, SCOPUS, Web of Science and Embase were searched for studies published between August 2015 and August 2025, in any language, addressing phage therapy in NTM-PD. Additional backward and forward citation searches were conducted to identify further relevant studies. RESULTS: Five studies met the inclusion criteria: four single-patient case reports and one small case series representing 20 unique patients treated with phage therapy. Of these, 18 had pulmonary NTM disease, mostly involving drug-resistant Mycobacterium abscessus infections treated under compassionate-use protocols or individualised regimens. Reported clinical and microbiological outcomes were inconsistent: some patients showed transient improvement or culture conversion, while others had no measurable benefit. Phage resistance was uncommon but incompletely assessed, and immune-mediated neutralisation emerged as a future concern. No serious adverse events were described. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports the feasibility but not the efficacy of phage therapy for NTM-PD. Published data are limited to isolated, heterogeneous cases and lack standardised definitions or controlled comparisons. Well-designed, prospective clinical trials are needed to clarify its therapeutic potential and optimise future application.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Intense influenza activity has been reported alongside the emergence of influenza A(H3N2) subclade K. While epidemiological studies have reported heterogeneous findings regarding public health impact, data remain lacking on its impact on clinical phenotype of people requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission. METHODS: Prospective, multicenter, observational SEVARVIR cohort study including people admitted in 42 French ICUs with laboratory-confirmed influenza infection during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons. Primary end point was day-28 mortality. RESULTS: Seven hundred twenty-six people were admitted for influenza in 2024-2025 (n = 360) and 2025-2026 (n = 366). In 2025-2026, influenza subtype was available for 265 people; 49% (n = 129) had A(H1N1)pdm09 and 51% (n = 136) had A(H3N2) subtype infection. Among the 40 people with A(H3N2) infection for whom whole-genome sequencing was available, 33 (82.5%) belonged to subclade K. In multivariable Cox analysis of the 2025-2026 season, age (adjusted hazard ratio, aHR = 1.04 [1.01;1.09]; P = .015), Clinical Frailty Scale (aHR = 1.59 [1.28;1.98]; P < .001), and sequential organ failure assessment score (aHR = 1.15 [1.05;1.26]; P = .003) were associated with an increased risk of death. In the 2024-2025/2025-2026 seasons or 2025-2026 season alone, influenza subtype was not associated with a significant risk of day-28 mortality. Phylogenetic analyses from our ICU cohort together with 600 contextual sequences from community-acquired influenza cases collected during the period showed no clustering according to severity. CONCLUSIONS: There was no evidence of an increased risk of death among critically ill people with influenza during the 2025-2026 season, despite the emergence of influenza A(H3N2) subclade K. papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: This study's purpose was to develop a prognostication model to predict persistent hypercapnia 3 months after discharge in patients hospitalized for COPD exacerbation and hypercapnia. METHODS: We developed the prediction model using a training data set comprising of participants in the RESCUE trial who received no ventilation support at home. We externally validated the model with a retrospective cohort. We calculated the rate of persistent hypercapnia 3 months post hospitalization according to the inpatient PaCO2. We also built regression models that included age and prior hospitalizations and calculated Area Under Curve (AUC). RESULTS: Our training cohort consisted of 69 participants. Among participants with baseline PaCO2 levels between 45 and 52mmHg, 59% had persistent hypercapnia at 3 months. It increased to 73.1% with PaCO2 between 53 and 60mmHg and 100% with greater than 60 mmHg (P < 0.001). Our regression model showed that for each one mmHg increase in baseline PaCO2 the 3-month PaCO2 increased by 0.41. The AUC was 0.779 (95%CI of 0.667 to 0.891). CONCLUSION: The last inpatient PaCO2 measurement may help predict persistent hypercapnia 3 months after discharge.

papers.title_en: Baloxavir and molnupiravir protect against severe influenza A(H5N1) infection in immunosuppressed hamsters.
papers.authors: Arroyave A, Rabezanahary H, Sahli A, Baz M
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Infectious and Immune Diseases, CHU de Québec Research Center, Québec, Québec, Canada.
papers.abstract_en: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses continue to expand their geographic and host range, raising concerns about zoonotic transmission and pandemic preparedness. Immunocompromised individuals often develop severe and prolonged disease, yet evidence guiding antiviral therapy remains limited. Here, we characterized the pathogenesis and assessed direct-contact transmission of an influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b genotype D1.1 virus recently isolated from a human case in British Columbia, Canada, in cyclophosphamide-immunosuppressed hamsters, with normal hamsters included for comparison of infection outcomes and viral shedding kinetics. We also evaluated the antiviral efficacy of oseltamivir (20 mg/kg twice daily for 5 days), baloxavir (50 mg/kg, 2 doses), and molnupiravir (50 or 200 mg/kg twice daily) as monotherapies or in combination (oseltamivir with low-dose molnupiravir) in immunosuppressed hamsters. While normal hamsters showed no mortality and achieved viral clearance, infection in immunosuppressed hamsters caused severe disease characterized by prolonged viral replication, neuroinvasion, and 75% mortality, with no direct-contact transmission detected. In the antiviral efficacy experiment, placebo-treated hamsters exhibited 50% mortality. Baloxavir resulted in 100% survival, shortened viral shedding, reduced viral replication and pulmonary inflammatory responses, and prevented neuroinvasion. High-dose molnupiravir also prevented mortality and achieved viral clearance in lung and brain tissues. Combination therapy resulted in 75% survival and similarly achieved viral clearance in both tissues, with reduced morbidity compared with oseltamivir and low-dose molnupiravir monotherapies. Oseltamivir resulted in 75% survival but failed to prevent severe clinical signs or reduce tissue viral titers, whereas low-dose molnupiravir showed outcomes comparable to placebo. These findings demonstrate the high pathogenicity of a human A(H5N1) isolate in immunosuppressed hamsters, support baloxavir as an effective therapeutic option, and identify molnupiravir-based regimens as promising strategies for severe influenza A(H5N1) infection.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Osimertinib is a standard first-line treatment for EGFR-mutant Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC), but acquired resistance remains a clinical challenge. Resistance involves genetic mechanisms and non-genetic cell-state transitions, including epithelial-to-mesenchymal (EMT) plasticity and drug-tolerant persister phenotypes. Patient-derived models established at disease progression may better capture clinically relevant resistance mechanisms. METHODS: We established LIBM-ADK-11 from the pleural effusion of a patient with EGFR exon 19p.Leu747_Pro753delinsSer-mutant NSCLC progressing on osimertinib. Cells were studied at low and high passages and fractionated by CD44 expression into CD44-positive/P2 and CD44-negative/P4 subpopulations. EGFR mutation status, CD44 expression, transcriptomics, growth, osimertinib sensitivity, EGFR signaling, sphere formation, cell-cycle distribution and pemetrexed response were evaluated. RESULTS: LIBM-ADK-11 retained the EGFR mutation during long-term culture. CD44 sorting identified two phenotypically distinct cell states. CD44-positive P2 cells were enriched for extracellular matrix remodeling, EMT-like, inflammatory, CAF-like and macrophage/TAM-mimicry programs, with increased glycolysis-related signatures, slower growth, higher metabolic activity and osimertinib resistance. CD44-negative P4 cells displayed a more epithelial profile, cholesterol-associated gene expression and greater osimertinib sensitivity. Osimertinib inhibited EGFR phosphorylation in both populations, indicating that P2 resistance was not explained by persistent EGFR signaling. Long-term culture favored loss of CD44-positive cells, whereas osimertinib delayed this loss and preferentially depleted the CD44-negative fraction. Pemetrexed partially reduced both compartments. CONCLUSIONS: LIBM-ADK-11 is a clinically relevant model of osimertinib-resistant EGFR-mutant NSCLC in which CD44-positive drug-tolerant and CD44-negative drug-sensitive states coexist. These findings highlight phenotypic heterogeneity as a potential determinant of osimertinib resistance and support strategies addressing distinct cellular states at disease progression.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Peak inspiratory flow (PIF) is a critical determinant of dry powder inhaler (DPI) effectiveness in managing patients with COPD. Suboptimal PIF may compromise drug delivery and clinical outcomes. The objective of the present study was to evaluate the association between repeated PIF measures and disease exacerbations, hospitalisations, and symptom burden in patients with stable COPD. METHODS: In this multi-country, observational cohort, 415 participants aged ≥40 years with confirmed COPD and a smoking history underwent PIF measurements at their prescribed inhaler's resistance, and low- and high-resistance levels using the In-Check DIAL G16. Clinical assessments occurred at 3 months (follow-up 1 (FU1)) and 6 months (follow-up 2 (FU2)) including spirometry, COPD Assessment Test scores, medication use and exacerbation/hospitalisation rates. RESULTS: At FU1, 29.4% (n=113/384) had typical suboptimal PIF and 28.6% (n=108/377) remained suboptimal at FU2. Participants with suboptimal PIF were more often female and current smokers, with consistently poorer lung function across both visits. Lower forced expiratory volume in 1 s (33.7±9.1% pred versus 45.7±9.2% pred, p=0.01), actual forced vital capacity and inspiratory capacity were observed. Suboptimal PIF significantly predicted moderate (p=0.03) and severe (p=0.01) exacerbations, was associated with higher hospitalisation risks (p=0.05) and with greater use of short-acting beta agonist, oral corticosteroid and triple therapy. CONCLUSIONS: Suboptimal PIF is a stable, clinically meaningful marker of worse COPD outcomes and may guide more personalised inhaler selection.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Malignant pleural effusions (MPE) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) are common and generally associated with a poor prognosis. Numerous studies have highlighted improved outcomes for NSCLC patients treated with targeted therapies, however these studies often utilize heterogenous populations of metastatic NSCLC. Our aim was to assess the overall survival of NSCLC patients with MPE and actionable biomarkers. METHODS: We reviewed patients with MPE related to lung cancer managed with indwelling tunneled pleural catheter (IPC) between 2008-2020. Demographics and advanced molecular testing results were reviewed to determine the presence of actionable biomarkers (EGFR=Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor, ALK=Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase, ROS=ROS Proto-Oncogene 1, PDL1=Programmed Death Ligand). Kaplan-Meier testing comparing overall survival per molecular testing results (positive/negative) was performed. RESULTS: A total of 129 patients with NSCLC and MPE undergoing IPC placement were identified. The median age was 70 (IQR - 61.5-80) years with a median survival of 87 (IQR - 32-266.5) days from IPC placement. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis demonstrated no significant association between molecular marker testing status (positive/negative) and overall survival (EGFR, p=0.70, ALK, p=0.50, ROS1, p=0.40, and PD-L1, p=0.40). CONCLUSION: Within a population of patients undergoing IPC placement for MPE management, the presence of targetable biomarkers was not associated with improved survival when compared to patients that did not have a targetable biomarker. Additional research is needed to explore the associations between outcomes in NSCLC patients with MPE and the presence of targetable biomarkers.

papers.abstract_en: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with increasing global burden driven by population growth and ageing, persistent harmful exposures, and substantial health inequities. The Lancet Commission on COPD articulated an ambitious vision for disease elimination with prevention, early detection, and intervention. This Review revisits that vision, assesses progress since 2022, and calls for a broader commitment to lifelong lung health as an update of the Commission. Across seven sections, this Review advances a unified framework integrating the biology of lung development and ageing, precision medicine, patient-centred outcomes, and regulatory reform. COPD is not a single, uniform disease; rather, a biologically complex condition shaped by genetic, developmental, environmental, infectious, and behavioural factors across the entire life course. Effective prevention and care should therefore move beyond the detection and treatment of late physiological impairment toward earlier disease recognition, biological stratification, and interventions to preserve lung health, reduce symptoms, and prevent morbidity and premature mortality. The Review charts a path from reactive, late-stage management toward proactive, equitable, precision-based prevention and care. The central premise is unequivocal: the global burden of COPD can be substantially reduced. Success should be measured not only by gains in lung function and survival but also by improvements in daily functioning, quality of life, and wellbeing. In this expanded vision, COPD is no longer viewed solely as a chronic disease to be managed but as a preventable and modifiable condition within a broader commitment to lifelong lung health.

papers.abstract_en: Digital health is increasingly embedded in cystic fibrosis (CF) care, spanning telehealth, mobile applications, remote monitoring, sensors, and data-driven decision support. Despite this rapid growth, CF digital health research remains fragmented, characterised by inconsistent terminology, disciplinary silos, and challenges in translating innovations into routine clinical practice. Many digital health technologies (DHTs) remain confined to small-scale pilots, while technological capability continues to outpace evaluation methodologies. This review applies the "eHealth evaluation cycle" as a structured framework to examine CF digital health research across the full development-to-implementation pathway. By mapping representative CF studies to the stages of conceptualisation, design and usability, feasibility, effectiveness, and implementation, the review highlights both strengths and gaps in the current evidence base. CF digital health research demonstrates notable maturity at the effectiveness stage, with several high-quality trials, but remains comparatively underdeveloped in early conceptual planning and late-stage implementation research. Adopting a life-cycle lens clarifies how evaluation methods should align with intervention maturity and supports more efficient and safer progression of DHTs. Moving forward, CF digital health research must prioritise structured early-phase development, rigorous feasibility work, and dedicated implementation studies to enable sustainable integration into clinical care.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The airway microbiome and host inflammatory response synergistically drive cystic fibrosis (CF) lung disease. We hypothesized that integrating airway microbial community structures with inflammatory biomarker profiles would reveal distinct ecological-inflammatory endotypes associated with clinical outcome measures. METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional secondary analysis of 112 clinically stable people with CF. Baseline sputum microbial communities were profiled via 16S rRNA sequencing, clustered using partitioning around medoids and linked with previously quantified inflammatory biomarker data. Co-occurrence network analyses assessed microbial community organisation. Associations with time-to-next pulmonary exacerbation (PEx) and 5-year prognostic survival scores were evaluated utilizing Cox proportional hazards models and multivariable regression. RESULTS: Two distinct ecological-inflammatory endotypes were identified. Endotype 1 (n = 65) exhibited higher microbial diversity, enrichment of oral-associated commensals (e.g., Prevotella, Veillonella), a highly interconnected co-occurrence network, and a moderated inflammatory milieu. Endotype 2 (n = 47) was characterized by Pseudomonas dominance, elevated neutrophilic inflammation (e.g., neutrophil elastase, IL-1β), and more advanced lung disease. The two-cluster solution was highly stable under repeated subsampling. Higher microbial diversity was independently associated with a more favourable 5-year prognostic survival score, including after adjustment for endotype membership. Endotype membership itself was not associated with time to subsequent PEx, and associations between ecological measures and PEx were attenuated after additional adjustment for baseline lung function. CONCLUSIONS: Distinct ecological-inflammatory endotypes in the CF airway reflect differences in microbial community structure, inflammatory state and underlying disease severity. Longitudinal studies are required to determine the stability of these states and their relationship with subsequent clinical disease.

papers.abstract_en: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) is common, frequently symptomatic, and closely associated with conditions already prioritised by the UK National Health Service (NHS), including obesity, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, cardiovascular disease, and stroke. Previous estimates suggest that approximately 8 million UK adults aged 30-69 years could have OSA, although the proportion remaining undiagnosed is uncertain. Evidence supports treatment benefits for daytime sleepiness, symptom burden, quality of life, driving safety, and blood pressure in some patients, but not a consistent reduction in major cardiovascular events. UK data indicate long diagnostic waits, regional variation, and gaps in follow-up. A proportionate NHS response should prioritise targeted case-finding within existing chronic-disease pathways, access to validated home-based diagnostics, specialist capacity for complex disease, and sustained treatment support. Implementation should be phased and evaluated prospectively for clinical outcomes, equity, workforce requirements, affordability, and budget impact.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: A large and increasing number of people are forcibly displaced worldwide because of war, food insecurity, and other crises. Streptococcus pneumoniae likely causes a substantial health burden in crisis-affected populations. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCVs) are widely used in routine immunisation programmes, including through the Essential Programme on Immunization (EPI) to protect against pneumococcal disease. They are typically administered as a three-dose schedule, either as three doses in early infancy or two doses in infancy followed by a booster at 9-18 months of age. However, PCVs are rarely used in humanitarian responses. We evaluated the potential impact of logistically feasible PCV campaigns in such settings. METHODS AND FINDINGS: We conducted a pneumococcal carriage, malnutrition, and social contact survey in a camp for displaced people near Hargeisa, Somaliland, to parameterise a transmission model accounting for migration. We projected the effect of PCV mass-vaccination campaigns using one or two doses and vaccinating children <1, 2, 5, 10, or 15 years (y) of age in the Somaliland camp and three different crisis settings. We found that a single-dose PCV campaign with high vaccine coverage in children <5 y or older can partially control vaccine-serotypes for up to 3 y, preventing 27% (95% CrI: 20, 34) of severe pneumococcal disease, defined as a composite of invasive pneumococcal disease and nonbacteraemic pneumonia, when vaccinating <5 y olds and 38% (95% CrI: 29, 46) when vaccinating <15 y olds. Expanded age eligibility is needed for comparable protection in settings with increased migration or more interaction with unvaccinated host populations. A campaign vaccinating <5 y olds is the most efficient use of PCV with 108 (95% CrI 77-162) vaccines needed to prevent one case of severe pneumococcal disease. Implementing such campaigns in displaced populations worldwide would require about 30 million doses in the next 5 y. Key limitations included sparse empirical data on PCV effectiveness and pneumococcal disease in humanitarian settings, and extrapolation of Somaliland carriage and contact patterns to other crisis settings. CONCLUSIONS: Single-dose mass-vaccination campaigns offer crisis-affected populations an effective, pragmatic immunisation strategy to deliver PCVs if routine EPI services have been disrupted.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To systematically review CT-based LAA% for emphysema quantification, explore the application of percentage low attenuation area (LAA% below -950HU), in comparison with visual emphysema scoring. METHODS: Following PRISMA-DTA guidelines, searches were conducted (01-01-1972 to 01-04-2026) in PubMed, Embase®, and Web of Science databases to identify English-language studies of adults ≥18 years with CT-quantified emphysema. Two independent readers screened titles, abstracts and full texts against predefined inclusion/exclusion criteria. Studies comparing LAA%-quantified emphysema with visual scores were included. RESULTS: 737 studies were reviewed, 5 (0.7%) met the eligibility criteria. These studies originated from Asia, Europe and the United States. LAA% cut-off values for emphysema varied: two studies used a 6% threshold, one used 5%, another used 1.5%, and one applied ordinal severity thresholds from 1% to 25%. Visual classification also differed, with three studies using the Fleischner Society system, one using a modified 3-point score, and another using the Goddard classification. Agreement between visual assessment and LAA%-based quantification was generally poor, with reported kappa values of 0.22 (n = 1,221), -0.06 (n = 200), and 0.48 (n = 98). Two studies further reported agreement based on sensitivity (86.8% and 58.0%) and specificity (84.2% and 39.0%). CONCLUSIONS: Based on limited evidence, substantial heterogeneity exists between visual assessment and LAA% quantification in emphysema. Discordance between visual and quantitative CT assessment likely reflects differences in diagnostic criteria and technical characteristics, highlighting the need for standardized reporting and methodology. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This systematic review provides a comprehensive comparison of visual scoring and LAA% metrics. It demonstrates limited agreement and substantial methodological heterogeneity of CT assessment of emphysema.

papers.abstract_en: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a devastating condition characterized by airflow limitation, inflammation, and structural lung damage. Metabolic dysregulation is recognized as a critical feature, but the key metabolic drivers remain unclear. This study identifies transaldolase1 (TALDO1) as a previously unrecognized metabolic regulator in cigarette smoke (CS)-induced COPD pathogenesis. TALDO1 is markedly upregulated in airway epithelial cells by CS exposure. Elevated TALDO1 promotes mitochondrial dysfunction, whereas its genetic knockdown attenuates CS-induced lung function decline and pulmonary inflammation. Mechanistically, TALDO1 activation redirects tryptophan metabolism toward the kynurenine pathway, leading to L-kynurenine accumulation. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of this pathway significantly alleviates mitochondrial damage, while L-kynurenine supplementation exacerbates injury. Treatment with the IDO inhibitor Epacadostat ameliorates CS-induced lung impairment and inflammation in vivo. These findings define a TALDO1-kynurenine-mitochondrial injury axis linking airway epithelial metabolic reprogramming to COPD, providing translational evidence for targeting this pathway as a therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract_en: Automated detection of pulmonary nodules on computed tomography has evolved from rule-based image processing algorithms to sophisticated artificial intelligence (AI) systems capable of nodule localisation, volumetric measurement and malignancy risk stratification. Four landmark papers published between 1994 and 1999 established the computational foundations of this field, introducing grey-level thresholding, morphological feature extraction, neural networks and three-dimensional analysis as core detection principles. We provide an overview of these foundational studies and trace the subsequent evolution of AI-based nodule detection, from early computer-aided detection systems to modern deep learning frameworks evaluated in the context of lung cancer screening programmes.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Airways Unit, Department of Respiratory Immunology, Toulouse University Hospital, Toulouse, France.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: COPD is the third leading cause of death worldwide. However, little is known about the characteristics of patients who die from COPD. The aim of this study was to determine the relationship between change or persistence in Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease group E (GOLD-E) status over time and COPD- and cardiovascular (CV)-related death. METHODS: Patients with COPD were identified by International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision (ICD-10) codes in the French national health insurance database. Patients who died from COPD or CV diseases between 1 January 2017 and 31 December 2022 were matched with living COPD patients. We performed a case-control analysis to compare the impact of the change in GOLD-E status between two periods: 13-24 months (period 2 (2026)) and 0-12 months (period 1 (2025)) prior to death or the index date. RESULTS: A total of 500 673 COPD patients died during the study period. Of these, 67 250 died from COPD and 41 585 from CV events. Of the patients whose deaths were COPD related, the proportion of patients with GOLD-E 2026 status increased between the two periods (58.3% versus 79.2%), but decreased in their matched living controls (58.3% versus 36.9%). Of the patients with GOLD-E 2026 status during period 2, becoming and remaining GOLD-E 2026 within their final 12 months was associated with COPD-related death (odds ratios 5.40 (95% CI 5.03-5.79) and 4.16 (95% CI 3.87-4.48), respectively; p<0.0001). INTERPRETATION: These data demonstrate that being GOLD-E for 2 years in a row is associated with a high risk of COPD-related death, of the same magnitude as being GOLD-E for 1 year.

papers.abstract_en: During chronic lung infections, Pseudomonas aeruginosa diversifies under selection from antibiotics, metabolic constraints, and host defenses. Macrophages are key sentinels of the innate immune system and play a central role in clearing airway pathogens. Yet, how they process heterogeneous bacterial populations remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate how P. aeruginosa evades phagocytosis under conditions that resemble chronic infection. We use an attenuated mutant lacking a functional type III secretion system (T3SS), which reduces macrophage killing, allowing us to isolate determinants of bacterial susceptibility to phagocytosis. Using transposon insertion sequencing (Tn-seq), we identify bacterial fitness factors under phagocytic selection. Our screen reveals that disruption of genes involved in swimming and twitching motility reduces uptake by macrophages. We find that defects in flagellar and type IV pili (T4P) function interfere with the physical interactions between bacteria and macrophages. Live-cell imaging shows that motility-deficient bacteria exhibit reduced surface accumulation and unstable attachment to macrophages, limiting their internalization. Clinical isolates with reduced swimming or twitching motility display similarly impaired uptake. We also test the influence of bacterial motility on macrophage survival by restoring T3SS activity in flagellar and T4P mutants. In the PAO1 background, most motility mutants retained the ability to kill macrophages indicating that cytotoxicity dominates bacteria-macrophage competition in the presence of a functional T3SS. However, the non-flagellated, hyper-piliated ΔfliCΔpilT mutant showed a surprisingly attenuated killing, which may reflect reduced bacterial encounters with macrophages, impaired engagement of cytotoxic effectors, or both. Together, our results show that swimming motility and type IV pili shape physical interactions between P. aeruginosa and macrophages, thereby influencing phagocytic uptake.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is characterized by vascular remodeling driven in part by apoptosis-resistant pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs). Na+/H+ exchanger isoform 1 (NHE1) regulates intracellular pH and plasma membrane cytoskeleton anchoring, but the role of NHE1 in PASMC apoptosis remains unclear. PASMCs were isolated from distal pulmonary arteries from control and Sugen/Hypoxia (SuHx) rats, a model of PH. NHE activity was measured via the ammonium pulse technique, protein via immunoblot, and apoptosis via Hoechst staining, Caspase-Glo® 3/7 Assay System and Annexin V/ propidium iodide immunofluorescence. NHE activity and NHE1 surface expression were increased in SuHx PASMCs compared to controls. Despite increased endoplasmic reticulum stress at baseline, SuHx PASMCs were resistant to apoptosis following hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) challenge. Inhibition of NHE activity with ethyl-isopropyl amiloride (EIPA) and NHE1 silencing with siRNA restored apoptosis in SuHx PASMCs. Conversely, NHE1 overexpression in control PASMCs conferred apoptosis resistance. Expression of mutant NHE1 constructs lacking ion translocation or ezrin binding also reduced H2O2-induced apoptosis. Mechanistically, H2O2 increased p38 phosphorylation (p-p38) in PASMCs from control, but not SuHx, rats, indicating impaired activation of this pro-apoptotic pathway. NHE1 suppression via EIPA or siRNA restored p-p38 in SuHx PASMCs, while overexpression of NHE1 (wild-type or mutants) suppressed p-p38 following apoptotic stimulation. Inhibition of p-p38 with SB203580 prevented the pro-apoptotic effect of EIPA, validating a role for p-p38 signaling in NHE1-mediated apoptosis resistance in SuHx PASMCs. These findings identify NHE1 as necessary and sufficient for PASMC apoptosis resistance in PH, by a mechanism involving suppression of p-p38.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Reduced exercise capacity in patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) is associated with poor prognosis. Oxygen pulse (O2 pulse) reflects exercise circulatory efficiency, but its determinants at submaximal exercise remain unclear. Phase angle (PhA) has recently emerged as a surrogate marker of muscle quality. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between lower-limb PhA and submaximal O2 pulse at the ventilatory threshold (VT), which reflects daily physical activity independent of maximal volitional effort, in patients with ILD. METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 111 patients with ILD enrolled in an educational hospitalization program (April 2024-March 2026). Among these, 35 patients completed cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). Lower-limb PhA was assessed via bioelectrical impedance analysis. The association between PhA and O2 pulse at VT was evaluated using Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis adjusted for age, %FVC, and tricuspid regurgitation velocity (TRV). RESULTS: The analyzed CPET sub-cohort (n = 35) had a mean age of 69.0 ± 8.4 years, 74.2% male, and %FVC of 85.3 ± 18.1%. Lower-limb PhA was significantly correlated with O2 pulse at VT (r = 0.629, p < 0.001). In multiple regression analysis, PhA remained independently associated with O2 pulse (β = 0.748, p = 0.001), with a model R2 of 0.433. CONCLUSIONS: Lower-limb PhA is an independent associated factor of O2 pulse in patients with mild-to-moderate ILD. Given the cross-sectional and retrospective nature of this study, these findings do not establish causality but suggest that muscle quality may be a relevant clinical indicator that warrants further prospective and interventional investigation.

papers.abstract_en: Cisplatin resistance remains a major therapeutic challenge in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Here, we investigated the antitumor effects and underlying mechanisms of Huayu Wan (HYW) in cisplatin-resistant ESCC. HYW markedly inhibited the growth of cisplatin-resistant human KYSE150 and murine mEC25 cells and induced a ferroptotic phenotype characterized by reactive oxygen species accumulation, increased intracellular iron, glutathione depletion, lipid peroxidation, and reduced GPX4 expression. Ferrostatin-1 partially reversed HYW-induced cytotoxicity. HYW also promoted immunogenic cell death-associated changes, including extracellular ATP and HMGB1 release and cell-surface calreticulin exposure. Mechanistically, HYW increased p53 expression and impaired the SLC7A11/GCLC-dependent cystine-glutathione antioxidant system, whereas GCLC overexpression and P53 inhibition partially restored redox homeostasis and cell survival. In parallel, HYW suppressed AKT-mTOR signaling and promoted NCOA4-associated ferritinophagy, as evidenced by increased NCOA4 and LC3-II and decreased FTH expression. Pharmacological inhibition of autophagy and NCOA4 knockdown attenuated iron accumulation and HYW-induced cytotoxicity. In cisplatin-resistant syngeneic tumors, HYW suppressed tumor growth with generally acceptable systemic tolerability, enhanced ferroptosis- and immunogenic stress-associated changes, reduced PD-L1 expression, and increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration. Moreover, HYW combined with anti-PD-1 treatment produced greater antitumor effects than either monotherapy. These findings suggest that HYW promotes ferroptosis through coordinated disruption of glutathione metabolism and NCOA4-associated ferritinophagy while enhancing antitumor immune responses in cisplatin-resistant ESCC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Extracellular adenosine triphosphate contributes to cough hypersensitivity through purinergic signalling, but airway purinergic biomarkers have not been well characterized in chronic cough. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility of measuring sputum adenosine triphosphate, adenosine, and CD39L1 and their relationship with cough outcomes. METHODS: In a prospective observational study, 100 adults with chronic cough were classified as chronic cough secondary to asthma or non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis (n=45) or refractory chronic cough (n=55) and received guideline-based treatment. Induced sputum was collected before and after treatment. Biomarkers were quantified using bioluminescence and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays and compared with 24-hour cough frequency, cough-specific quality of life, and cough severity. RESULTS: Baseline biomarker concentrations were similar between groups. In refractory chronic cough, lower sputum adenosine triphosphate and higher CD39L1 were associated with worse patient-reported cough outcomes, whereas no associations were observed in chronic cough secondary to asthma or non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis. Sputum adenosine triphosphate decreased following treatment in the overall cohort and in chronic cough secondary to asthma or non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis, while adenosine and CD39L1 remained unchanged. Changes in biomarkers were not associated with clinical improvement. CONCLUSION: Purinergic biomarkers can be measured in induced sputum. Lower adenosine triphosphate and higher CD39L1 were associated with worse cough outcomes in refractory chronic cough. CLINICAL IMPLICATION: Measurement of airway purinergic biomarkers may help identify neuronal dysfunction and support the development of targeted therapies for refractory chronic cough. papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Adherence to center-based pulmonary rehabilitation after a COPD-related hospitalization-which improves all outcomes, including survival-is only 3%. Home-based programs have been proposed as a more feasible option, but they are not systematically offered, and patient preference is unknown. OBJECTIVES AND METHODS: This pragmatic randomized trial involving patients with COPD recently hospitalized for a COPD exacerbation, originally aimed to investigate the comparative effect two arms: The choice of a facilitated referral to a center-based outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation program or a home-based program versus a home-based program on adherence to post-hospitalization rehabilitation and disease-specific QoL measured by the Chronic Respiratory Questionnaire. The trial aimed to investigate the patient's preference of home vs center-based rehabilitation in individuals randomized to the choice arm. Daily steps were measured by Actigraph ®.The asynchronous home-based program included weekly health coaching and daily monitoring of daily steps, symptoms, and a 20-minute daily flexibility-balance exercise routine. RESULTS: Of 1,906 patients approached, 294 (15%) were randomized and agreed to the rehabilitation options offered by the study arms (uptake); of those, 56% completed the 12-week intervention (adherence). Of the 145 randomized to the choice arm, only one patient chose center-based PR; therefore, both groups received the same intervention, and results are presented as a one-group (before-after) analysis. Compared with baseline, the home intervention significantly improved (p < 0.01) physical and emotional QoL (Chronic Respiratory Questionnaire) and increased daily steps beyond the minimal clinically important difference. Trajectory models adjusted for age, FEV1%, and mMRC (breathlessness) confirmed sustained improvements in QoL at 6 and 12 months from baseline. CONCLUSIONS: When offered a choice of rehabilitation setting after a COPD-related hospital admission for an exacerbation, home-based rehabilitation is patients' preferred option. Sustained quality-of-life improvements in 1 year may represent an opportunity to regain well-being and/or deliver primary palliative care. Our results may have important implications for clinical practice.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains a life-threatening pulmonary condition with persistently high mortality rates. Echinacoside (ECH) is a natural compound that has shown protective effects in experimental acute lung injury; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying its effects in ARDS remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to explore the potential mechanisms underlying the protective role of ECH in ARDS. METHODS: The protective effect of ECH on ARDS mice was evaluated. Subsequently, network pharmacology combined with RNA-sequencing was employed to identify mechanisms modulated by ECH. Finally, the mechanism of ECH on ARDS was verified in ARDS mice and mouse lung epithelial cells. RESULTS: ECH reduced the level of inflammatory response and alleviated lung injury in ARDS mice. Network pharmacology and RNA sequencing results suggested that its mechanism may be related to regulating inflammatory response, anti-oxidative stress, and inhibiting cell death. Further experiments indicated that ECH inhibited ferroptosis and pyroptosis, possibly through regulation of the KEAP1/NRF2 axis. Molecular dynamics, molecular docking, and protein-small molecule interaction verification demonstrated that ECH binds to the Kelch/DGR domain of KEAP1. CONCLUSIONS: ECH binds to KEAP1 and may interfere with the KEAP1-NRF2 interaction, thereby promoting NRF2 release, which subsequently suppresses cellular pyroptosis and ferroptosis, ultimately reducing inflammation and lung injury. These findings support further investigation of ECH as a potential strategy for ARDS.
