papers.abstract_en: Asymptomatic tuberculosis is a major but incompletely defined manifestation of the tuberculosis disease spectrum and an important challenge for active case finding. It is best understood as a symptom-defined and method-dependent phenotype rather than a uniform biological stage. Individuals classified as asymptomatic may have minimal or extensive radiographic abnormalities, low or intermittent bacillary shedding, or clinically inapparent disease that remains stable, regresses, fluctuates, or progresses. Differences in terminology, symptom ascertainment, population risk and diagnostic intensity have therefore led to substantial variation in how asymptomatic or subclinical tuberculosis is recognized and interpreted across studies and programmes. This Review examines current and emerging approaches for diagnosing asymptomatic tuberculosis, with emphasis on the interaction between epidemiological risk, radiological detectability, microbiological confirmation and longitudinal follow-up. Symptom-based screening and passive case finding miss a substantial proportion of bacteriologically or radiographically evident tuberculosis. Conventional sputum-based testing is constrained by difficulty obtaining specimens, paucibacillary disease, intermittent shedding and imperfect sensitivity. Chest radiography and computer-aided detection can expand screening capacity and standardize triage, but they cannot independently establish disease activity or exclude tuberculosis. Computed tomography and positron emission tomography/computed tomography provide more sensitive characterization in selected settings, although their cost, accessibility and limited specificity preclude routine use. Non-sputum pathogen assays and host biomarkers are promising because they may reduce dependence on spontaneous sputum, but most remain insufficiently validated, and their incremental clinical or programmatic value over imaging-based triage and conventional confirmation remains uncertain. The diagnostic challenge of asymptomatic tuberculosis lies not simply in the absence of symptoms, but in the unstable boundary between infection, early disease, radiological abnormality, microbiological detectability and future risk. Clinical and public health practice should therefore move beyond single-test strategies toward staged, risk-stratified diagnostic pathways that integrate symptom ascertainment, exposure risk, imaging, confirmatory microbiology, enhanced specimen collection and longitudinal reassessment. Such pathways should be viewed as flexible clinical-programmatic frameworks for organizing diagnostic uncertainty, guiding multidisciplinary decisions and generating testable hypotheses, rather than as validated treatment algorithms.

papers.title_en: Mycobacterium abscessus induces immune suppression in cystic fibrosis macrophages.
papers.authors: Hill PJ, Miller CJ, Rascon R, Clary G, Idosa AW, Gavrilin MA, McCoy KS, Amer AO et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Microbial Infection & Immunity, The Ohio State University, Columbus, OH, United States.
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: People with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) are highly susceptible to chronic lung infections with Mycobacterium abscessus (MAB), a nontuberculous mycobacterium (NTM) that is intrinsically resistant to antibiotics. While macrophage dysfunction is recognized in CF, responses to MAB in primary human macrophages remain poorly defined. METHODS: We investigated the innate immune response to MAB using peripheral blood monocytes and monocyte-derived macrophages from pwCF and healthy donors. Macrophages were infected with opsonized smooth (MAS) or rough (MAR) isolates of MAB morphotypes at low multiplicity of infection. After removal of extracellular bacteria, intracellular burden, oxidative burst, NOX2 activation, and cytokine production were assessed at 2- and 24-hours post-infection. RESULTS: MAB uptake was comparable across all groups and non-CF macrophages showed no difference in intracellular MAR or MAS at 24h. In contrast, CF macrophages harbored significantly more intracellular MAR at 24 hours, a phenotype recapitulated by CFTR knockdown in non-CF macrophages. MAB-infected CF macrophages demonstrated a significantly reduced oxidative burst and diminished NOX2 p47phox phosphorylation. Non-CF macrophages treated with CFTR inhibitor mimicked the reduced oxidative burst. CF macrophages also exhibited an altered cytokine response with significantly elevated IL-8 but decreased IL-1β relative to healthy macrophages. Notably, MAR-infected CF macrophages secreted significantly less TNF-α compared with non-CF macrophages and exhibited markedly reduced apoptosis compared with MAR-infected non-CF and MAS-infected CF macrophages. DISCUSSION: These findings demonstrate that CF macrophages are intrinsically impaired in their ability to control the virulent rough MAB morphotype, highlighting a potential mechanism for persistent NTM infection in pwCF and underscoring the need for host-directed therapies.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Drug-resistant tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia. This study aimed to characterize the genetic diversity, lineage distribution, and genotypic resistance profiles of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates across the Indonesian archipelago using whole-genome sequencing. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted using 1,281 analyzed MTB isolates derived from the 2017-2018 National Tuberculosis Drug Resistance Survey (DRS TB). Samples were screened via Xpert MTB/RIF and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing using the MGIT 960 system. Genomic DNA was extracted using the CTAB protocol. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) libraries were prepared using the Nextera XT DNA Library Preparation Kit (Illumina, San Diego, CA, USA). Sequencing was performed on an Illumina MiSeq platform using the MiSeq Reagent Kit v3 (600 cycles), generating paired-end reads of 2 × 300 bp. To identify drug resistance-associated mutations and determine strain lineage/sub-lineages, raw sequencing reads were initially processed with Trimmomatic. The filtered reads were subsequently aligned to the Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv reference genome (ATCC 27294;NC_000962.3) using the MTBseq pipeline, which the BWA-MEM algorithm (v0.7.17) for sequence mapping. Variant calling was carried out with Samtools mpileup (v1.6). RESULTS: Four major MTB lineages were identified: Lineage 4 (43.1%) was dominant, followed by Lineage 2 (30.4%) and Lineage 1 (26.3%), while Lineage 3 was rare, with only 0.16% detected. At the sub-lineage level, L2.2.1 (18.5%), L1.2.1 (11.3%), and L4.1.2.1 (9.7%) were the most prevalent. Resistance to first-line drugs was the most frequent, primarily driven by mutations in the katG p.Ser315Thr (7.5%) and rpoB p.Ser450Leu (5%), conferring isoniazid and rifampicin resistance, respectively. Second-line resistance was highest for Fluoroquinolones (2.03%). Notably, four pre-XDR strains (0.31%) were identified and validated across Java-Bali and Sumatera, all harboring critical gyrA mutations and rpoB mutations (p.Asp435Tyr, p.Asn437Asp, p.Ser450Leu, and p.Ser450Trp). CONCLUSION: The study confirms a high prevalence of L2 and L4 in Indonesia. The identification of pre-XDR-TB isolates among the national survey samples highlights an urgent need for expanded molecular surveillance. While newer drugs like Bedaquiline remain effective, the presence of specific gyrA mutations underscores the necessity of integrating WGS into national TB control programs to proactively manage resistance and optimize treatment regimens.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Vagal sensory neurons that innervate the airways signal the detected noxious information to the brain to produce a perceptible sensation called urge-to-cough as well as reflex and behavioural coughing. Understanding the central neural mechanisms in regulating airway sensory processing is important for the development of more effective therapeutic options for conditions such as chronic cough. METHODS: In this pilot study, healthy volunteers (n=14) inhaled nebulised capsaicin at a personalised maximum concentration for induction of a strong level of urge-to-cough without coughing. Magnetoencephalography (MEG) was employed to directly detect regional neural activity changes in the brain accompanying capsaicin-evoked urge-to-cough sensations. RESULTS: The neural activity in delta and high gamma bands increased with an increase in capsaicin-evoked urge-to-cough in multiple higher order brain regions such as the insula, the cerebellum, the thalamus, the putamen and the brainstem areas, including the medullary nuclei where airway-innervating vagal sensory neurons are known to terminate. CONCLUSION: For the first time, we have established the feasibility and utility of MEG for examining the brain control of coughing. We show that the neural activity in delta and high gamma bands in multiple brain regions including medullary nuclei is involved in processing of urge-to-cough, confirming previous findings with functional magnetic resonance imaging.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Pneumonia is one of the deadliest lower respiratory tract infections worldwide, and rapidly distinguishing bacterial pneumonia, viral pneumonia, and normal chest radiographs is crucial for guiding precise medication and avoiding misdiagnosis. However, the imaging manifestations of bacterial and viral pneumonia on chest X-rays often overlap, and some normal chest X-rays may also show atypical changes. Clinical differentiation relies heavily on the expertise of senior physicians. In primary care or emergency settings where experienced radiologists are scarce, this can readily lead to diagnostic delays and antibiotic misuse, further exacerbating the risk of antimicrobial resistance and severe outcomes. METHODS: To address this challenge, this study proposes a lightweight network named FLIFuse. By adopting a parallel multi-branch architecture, the model thoroughly mines discriminative imaging features, substantially reducing computational overhead while maintaining high classification accuracy. This provides a technical solution that balances accuracy and efficiency for medical image analysis in resource-constrained environments. FLIFuse consists of three heterogeneous branches: an ExtraDW module that enhances local texture details, a Conv2Next module that captures global semantic structures, and an FLI Block that fuses multi-granularity information across different receptive fields to strengthen the response in critical regions. RESULTS: The model occupies only 33.43 M parameters and incurs a computational cost of 6.61 GFLOPs. On the public ChestXRay2017 dataset, FLIFuse achieves a three-class classification accuracy of 91.4% for normal, bacterial pneumonia, and viral pneumonia, outperforming several current state-of-the-art models and attaining extremely low resource consumption while ensuring diagnostic accuracy. In cross-domain tests on an external COVID-19 chest X-ray dataset and the Nerthus endoscopic image dataset, the model also exhibits stable transferability, demonstrating its potential for cross-domain adaptation across different medical imaging tasks. DISCUSSION: These results demonstrate that FLIFuse strikes a favorable balance between diagnostic accuracy and computational efficiency, providing an efficient and lightweight model option for computer-aided interpretation of pneumonia imaging, and showing potential for translation into clinical auxiliary diagnosis.

Intravenous phages were administered at 109 plaque forming units per dose and nebulised phages at 5 × 109 plaque forming units per dose twice daily. Within two days, marked elevations in alanine transaminase, aspartate transaminase, alkaline phosphatase, and gamma glutamyl transferase developed, prompting treatment cessation. Peak alanine transaminase reached 494 U/L and alkaline phosphatase 527 U/L were observed, while bilirubin and coagulation parameters remained normal. Extensive investigation, including magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography and medication review, identified no alternative cause. Rechallenge with nebulised phage therapy alone resulted in recurrent liver enzyme elevation after eight days, again resolving following discontinuation. Temporal correlation was demonstrated between liver function test abnormalities and detection of phage DNA in serum and sputum. No bacteriophage neutralisation, bacterial DNAaemia, development of phage resistance, or significant bacterial genomic change was observed. Despite early cessation, lung function improved over the subsequent six months.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Allergic and type 2 (T2) inflammatory biomarkers are increasingly used to predict outcomes and guide treatment in asthma and COPD. The objective of this cross-sectional study was to determine the prevalence of allergic sensitisation and T2 biomarkers and their clinical associations among patients with diagnoses of asthma and/or COPD in NOVELTY, a large multinational, observational study. METHODS: Participants were enrolled from primary/specialist care, stratified by physician-assigned diagnosis and severity. We assessed fractional exhaled nitric oxide (≥25 ppb), blood eosinophils (≥300 cells·µL-1) and allergen-specific IgE sensitisation (≥0.35 kU·L-1 to any of 11 aeroallergens). Associations between biomarkers and clinical outcomes were examined using descriptive statistics and multivariable regression models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index and smoking status. RESULTS: Data for all biomarkers were available for 4352 participants (asthma: n=2194; asthma+COPD: n=633; COPD: n=1525). Overall, 63% participants had at least one positive biomarker (asthma: 77%; asthma+COPD: 60%; COPD: 45%); only 8%, 4% and 1% of participants, respectively, were positive for all three biomarkers. Women and current smokers were more likely to be triple-negative. Among participants with asthma, having more positive biomarkers was associated with more severe physician-assessed disease, lower lung function and exacerbations. By contrast, in COPD, having no positive biomarkers was associated with more severe physician-assessed disease and lower lung function. CONCLUSIONS: Allergic and T2 biomarkers are highly prevalent in asthma and asthma+COPD but less frequent in COPD. Their patterns show distinct associations, sometimes with opposite trends, across diagnostic groups, suggesting distinct underlying mechanisms that differ.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health challenge in Malawi. While diagnostic pathways are well established, less is known about how people experience repeated care-seeking and diagnostic uncertainty before receiving a TB diagnosis. OBJECTIVE: To explore pre-diagnostic TB experiences and care-seeking among adults with TB and caregivers of children with TB in urban Blantyre, Malawi. METHODS: We conducted in-depth interviews with 14 participants in urban Blantyre, Malawi (five male patients, five female patients, and four female caregivers acting as proxies for pediatric TB patients under 11 years). Data were coded deductively and inductively, then analyzed using a framework approach. Social Cognitive Theory informed the interview guide, and Candidacy Theory informed interpretation of access to TB investigation across multiple healthcare encounters. RESULTS: Participants described prolonged, distressing pre-diagnostic journeys, with early symptoms of TB frequently misattributed to malaria or minor respiratory conditions. As symptoms persisted, participants reported repeatedly seeking care, often attending health facilities multiple times before TB testing was initiated. These encounters did not provide immediate diagnostic resolution and represented participant-reported opportunities for earlier TB investigation. Participants' social networks shaped decision-making along the pathway, occasionally reinforcing misattribution but often prompting escalation to formal care. Repeated unresolved encounters imposed substantial economic burden on participants and their families, including loss of income, business disruption, and increased reliance on family support. CONCLUSION: In urban Malawi, participants described TB diagnostic pathways shaped by symptom uncertainty, social and material circumstances, and repeated healthcare encounters without timely diagnostic resolution. The findings highlight the potential value of reassessing persistent or worsening symptoms during repeat encounters. Strengthening such reassessment may support integrated, patient-centered TB care and reduce avoidable socioeconomic burden.

papers.abstract_en: Endobronchial carcinoid tumor rarely causes secondary spontaneous pneumothorax. We report a female in her 30s who reported progressive decline in her overall exercise tolerance with dyspnea on exertion and frequent upper respiratory infections (URIs) for 2 years presented for persistent spontaneous pneumothorax (SP). Initially, she presented to the emergency department (ED) for concerns of cough with mild hemoptysis and congestion for 2 weeks. She was found to have a small left-sided pneumothorax. She was admitted and treated for community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). Post-hospital follow-up showed a persistent pneumothorax unchanged in size. She was followed for weeks with serial chest X-rays, which later showed an increased size of the pneumothorax. She was admitted, and a chest tube was placed. Later, bronchoscopy was done, which showed near complete occlusion of the left mainstem bronchus by an endobronchial lesion. Pathology results showed a well-differentiated neuroendocrine grade 1 tumor consistent with carcinoid. She was successfully treated with tumor resection and photodynamic therapy (PDT). This case highlighted an unusual presentation of an endobronchial carcinoid tumor that requires further diagnostic workup with appropriate intervention.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung and prostate cancers remain leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, driven by inflammation-mediated tumour progression and hormone-dependent signalling. IL-1R1 promotes chronic inflammation, metastasis, and tumour survival, while androgen receptor (AR) signalling is a central driver of prostate cancer growth. Simultaneous targeting of inflammatory and androgenic pathways represents a promising strategy to overcome therapeutic resistance. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate natural compounds derived from Aconitum heterophyllum (atisine, linoleic acid) and Podophyllum hexandrum (podophyllotoxin), as modulators of IL-1R1 and AR using integrated experimental and computational approaches. METHODS: Phytochemicals were extracted from tuberous roots of A. heterophyllum and fruits of P. hexandrum using Soxhlet extraction and isolated by TLC and column chromatography. Cytotoxicity and long-term antiproliferative effects were assessed using MTT and colony formation assays in A549 (lung) and LNCaP (prostate) cancer cell lines. Computational analyses included ADMET profiling, molecular docking against IL-1R1 (PDB: 1ITB) and AR (PDB: 2YHD), 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, MM-GBSA binding free-energy calculations, network pharmacology-based target and pathway enrichment analyses. RESULTS: Podophyllotoxin exhibited potent cytotoxicity with IC50 values of 0.04 µM in both A549 and LNCaP cells, outperforming doxorubicin, while atisine showed moderate activity (IC50: 2.1-2.3 µM). Linoleic acid displayed weak anticancer activity (IC50 >100 µM). Colony formation assays confirmed strong suppression of clonogenic survival by podophyllotoxin and a moderate inhibitory effect by atisine. Docking studies suggested favorable binding affinities (-8.1 to -5.9 kcal/mol), and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable protein-ligand complexes with low RMSD fluctuations. ADMET analysis supported favorable drug-likeness for atisine and podophyllotoxin. Network pharmacology identified 133 intersecting targets, with key hub genes including SRC, EGFR, and AKT1, enriched in PI3K-Akt and cancer-related signaling pathways. CONCLUSION: Atisine and podophyllotoxin exhibited significant anticancer activity and demonstrated favorable predicted interactions with the Interleukin-1 receptor type 1 (IL-1R1) and Androgen Receptor (AR), suggesting their potential as dual modulators that warrant further experimental validation. Their promising anticancer profile was supported by strong cytotoxicity, favorable predicted protein-ligand interactions, acceptable pharmacokinetic properties, and multitarget network pharmacology analyses. These findings provide a preliminary foundation for further optimization and in vivo validation toward the development of novel anticancer therapeutics targeting inflammation-driven and androgen-dependent cancers.

papers.abstract_en: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by persistent pulmonary inflammation and tissue remodeling, yet the cellular states and regulatory mechanisms underlying monocyte functional heterogeneity remain incompletely understood. Here, we generate a high-resolution single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the human respiratory system and identify a diverse monocyte functional landscape in healthy lungs containing a HSPA1B+ inflammatory monocytes state. This population exhibits enhanced inflammatory programs, cytokine and chemokine activity, and shows a distinct position within the inferred transcriptional landscape of the continuous monocyte functional spectrum. Cell-cell communication analysis further reveals that HSPA1B+ inflammatory monocytes function as active communication nodes within a stromal-immune-vascular network, integrating MIF, extracellular matrix, and immune-regulatory signals while mediating CXCL and adhesion-associated interactions with surrounding cellular compartments. Comparative analysis of COPD lung tissues and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid demonstrates selective enrichment of this inflammatory monocyte program in disease-associated environments, whereas peripheral blood monocytes from healthy individuals and COPD patients show limited representation of this state. Integrated transcriptomic and m6A regulator-associated analyses identify WTAP, a core component of the m6A methyltransferase complex, as a factor associated with the inflammatory monocytes program. WTAP silencing in inflammatory monocyte models suppresses pro-inflammatory mediators while enhancing interferon-response and antigen-presentation programs. Collectively, these findings define an inflammatory monocyte state landscape in the human respiratory system and identify a WTAP-associated transcriptional program linked to monocyte inflammatory activation and functional remodeling in COPD. This study provides new insights into the organization of pulmonary immune states and the potential regulatory mechanisms underlying chronic inflammatory regulation in COPD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with severe uncontrolled asthma (SUA) and a T2 eosinophilic phenotype exhibit variable response to biologic therapy (BT). Currently, accurate biomarkers predicting this response are lacking. We aimed to explore whether microRNA (miRNA) and messenger RNA (mRNA) profiles in bronchial biopsies (BB) may help identify patients achieving a complete clinical response after 6 months of BT. AIMS: To explore whether BB miRNA and mRNA profiles may be associated with clinical response to BT in SUA population. METHODS: Thirty-four consecutive SUA patients with a T2 high phenotype were characterized and underwent bronchoscopy with BB before initiating anti-IL-5/5R BT. Clinical response was evaluated 6 months later. Both, miRNA and mRNA were extracted from BB, and their expression profiles were analyzed via microarrays. Gene Ontology and KEGG pathway analyses were performed to understand the biological functions and signaling pathways involved. RESULTS: After BT, 64% showed complete clinical response, 18% patients were non-responders, and 18% obtained a partial response. Comparing non-responders vs. responders showed 35 differentially expressed mRNAs, and 8 miRNAs in BB samples. Integrated analysis of miRNA and mRNA data suggested that three key genes (FOXO1, ZBTB16 and OLFML3) may be involved in asthma pathogenesis. CONCLUSIONS: Expression patterns between responders and non-responders to BT appeared to differ in BB of SUA patients, highlighting the involvement of multiple pathways related to airway inflammation and airway remodeling. Our results provide preliminary evidence suggesting that FOXO1, ZBTB16 and OLFML3 might be involved in the biological response to anti-IL-5/5R therapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a life-threatening respiratory condition characterized by uncontrolled pulmonary inflammation and epithelial barrier dysfunction. Zang-Si-Wei Qingfei Mixture (ZSW) is a promising Tibetan herbal formula used clinically to alleviate pulmonary symptoms, yet its pharmacological targets and therapeutic pathways in ALI have not been fully explored. This study aims to identify the bioactive constituents of ZSW and elucidate their protective and therapeutic mechanisms in ALI. METHODS: ZSW's components were identified via liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) previously and network pharmacology. Target affinity was evaluated using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. In vivo, C57BL/6J mice with lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ALI were used to evaluate the pretreatment and post-treatment effects of ZSW and its core component, Ellagic Acid (EA). In vitro, MLE-12 cells and the PI3K/mTOR dual inhibitor BEZ235 were utilized to investigate the role of PI3K/AKT signaling and NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis. RESULTS: EA was identified as ZSW's core bioactive constituent, demonstrating high binding stability with AKT1, PIK3CA, and PIK3R1. In vivo, ZSW and EA significantly attenuated lung histological damage, edema, and alveolar-capillary hyperpermeability. Both markedly reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6 and IL-1β) in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Mechanistically, ZSW and EA inhibited PI3K and AKT phosphorylation and were accompanied by decreased NLRP3 inflammasome-associated proteins (decreased NLRP3, ASC, and cleaved Caspase-1) and GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis (decreased GSDMD-N and lactate dehydrogenase release). Notably, the 6-h post-LPS therapeutic model showed that both treatments effectively reversed established lung injury. CONCLUSION: ZSW and EA exert anti-inflammatory and lung-protective effects, accompanied by modulation of PI3K/AKT signaling and suppression of NLRP3 inflammasome-associated pyroptosis. This provides robust scientific evidence for ZSW's clinical application and highlights EA as a promising therapeutic candidate for acute inflammatory lung diseases.

papers.abstract_en: The continuous emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants (e.g., JN.1, KP.3) and the significantly elevated risk of severe COVID-19 in patients with rheumatic autoimmune diseases highlight an urgent unmet clinical need for dual-targeted therapeutics. Daphnetin (7,8-dihydroxycoumarin), a natural coumarin compound with a long history of clinical use in China, prevents SARS-CoV-2 infection by downregulating the viral entry receptor ACE2 through inhibition of HIF-1α and JAK2/STAT3 signaling. This review synthesizes the pleiotropic pharmacological mechanisms of daphnetin, including anti-inflammatory (NF-κB, JAK/STAT, NLRP3), antioxidant (Nrf2/Keap1), immunomodulatory (Th17/Treg balance), and mitochondrial protective pathways. These pathways are critically involved in the pathogenesis of both severe COVID-19 and rheumatic diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). We propose that daphnetin represents a novel "one agent, dual protection" strategy: it not only blocks viral entry by reducing ACE2 but also mitigates the hyperinflammatory and oxidative stress states that exacerbate both COVID-19 severity and rheumatic disease activity. Given its established safety, oral activity, and low cost, daphnetin is a promising candidate for clinical translation in high-risk comorbid populations. Key unresolved questions and future research directions are also discussed.
